strategy.headline: Oakland is the soul, San Francisco the address: win the Bay on the bridge between them, in gear built for fog.
strategy.thesis: Dub Nation is a two-city fan base: the team played 47 seasons in Oakland before moving to Chase Center in 2019, and Oakland, which also lost the Raiders and A's, still sets the taste while San Francisco and Silicon Valley supply the spend. Curry's Under Armour partnership ended in late 2025 and his next shoe partner is unconfirmed, so Nike's sure lane today is the team (Specter, City Edition, apparel) and the Bay's own makers, with Curry as the single biggest upside to watch rather than build on. After a 37-45 season and a 40.5 win total, demand runs on heritage, the dynasty-era window and a winter calendar (the Oct 21 ESPN game at the Lakers, Cup Fridays, the Christmas nightcap against Denver) rather than a playoff run. Nike wins by telling the Bay Bridge story honestly, launching in Oakland first, paying Black, Latino, Chinese and Filipino-American creators with credit and approval rights, and dressing fans for 50-degree fog nights instead of selling them another jersey.

archetype.name: The Dynasty Diaspora
archetype.description: A fan base forged in 40 lean Oakland years and spoiled by four titles, now spread across The Town, The City and the 408. It is loyal to Curry, Draymond and Kerr more than to an arena, and it is nostalgic for Oracle in a building that never had Oracle's soul.

pulse.teamMoment: Curry's aging core ran it back after a 37-45 season, a play-in win over the Clippers and a 111-96 loss at Phoenix: the Warriors chased Giannis and Anthony Davis without a deal, re-signed Porzingis, Horford, Melton and Gary Payton II, added Niang and Brandon Williams, drafted Yaxel Lendeborg at No. 11, and have Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody recovering from injury.
pulse.sentiment: Grateful and anxious: fans are invested in the dynasty-era window but expect little (a 40.5 win total, with previews doubting a play-in spot), so the mood favors keepsake and heritage buying over hype.

topInsights.title: The logo already picked the Bay Bridge, not the Golden Gate
topInsights.insight: The Warriors' roundel shows the Bay Bridge, the span joining The City to The Town; it opened Nov 12, 1936, turns 90 during Cup group play, and Chase Center sits a short walk from its western approach. The Golden Gate is the tourist bridge to Marin, and its orange next to navy echoes the disliked 1997-2010 era.
topInsights.implication: Make Bay Bridge cable lines, catenaries and paired City/Town lettering the spine of Bay product, drawn from public geometry by a credited letterer. Hold Golden Gate orange (#C0362C) to small accents and never lead with navy and orange.

topInsights.title: Oakland sets the taste, San Francisco pays the bill
topInsights.insight: Hyphy, scraper bikes, turf dancing, Oaklandish and the We Believe memory all come from the East Bay. The Chase Center buyer is premium, tech-paid and San Francisco-based, and Oakland reads SF-only product as the team that left.
topInsights.implication: Sequence every Bay drop Oakland-first: an Oakland maker's name on the tag and an Oakland pop-up (Uptown, Lake Merritt, Fox Theater) before Chase Center and Union Square. Tier the same story from accessible East Bay tees to premium Mission Bay pieces.

topInsights.title: Nike's lane is the team while Curry's shoe deal is open
topInsights.insight: Curry's Under Armour partnership ended in late 2025, Curry Brand is independent, and reports have him as a sneaker free agent with Nike among interested brands, none of it confirmed. The franchise's most emotional face is therefore an open question, while the uniform wardrobe (Specter, City, Icon) and team apparel are Nike's for certain.
topInsights.implication: Build the season on team-level product and franchise stories (Bay Bridge, We Believe, Run TMC, 1975, Strength in Numbers), with no Curry likeness, 'Night Night' or No. 30 hero use and no Curry-linked causes until his partner is confirmed. If it is Nike, the dynasty-window story becomes the lead; if a rival, it stays off.

topInsights.title: This is a winter-only year
topInsights.insight: After a play-in exit and with a 40.5 win total, the April-June peak that usually carries Warriors retail is not guaranteed. The money is in the Oct 21 ESPN game at the Lakers, Cup Fridays from Oct 30, the Black Friday run and Dec 25 against Denver at Chase Center (7:30 p.m. PT), in Dungeness crab season.
topInsights.implication: Front-load existing in-line product into October-December and treat new Bay-specific pieces this winter as small local pilots, since full Nike development runs many months ahead. Build spring playoff gear as a contingent 48-hour fast-turn, not a committed buy.

topInsights.title: Fog is the product brief
topInsights.insight: Chase Center nights sit in the 50s with wind off the bay, the season runs through atmospheric-river rain, and locals layer (fleece or quarter-zip under a light shell, hood up) rather than wearing parkas. Hoodies, warm-ups and shells sell most of the year, and shorts get a narrow September-October window.
topInsights.implication: Make a fog-gray layering system (packable shell, midweight half-zip, vest, beanie) cut to sit over a jersey the Warriors' volume engine, in true women's and youth fits, styled on BART riders and Thrive City crowds rather than the tech-vest look locals mock.

topInsights.title: Asian American heritage is core business, not a theme night
topInsights.insight: Asian Americans are more than a third of San Francisco and Santa Clara County, SoMa Pilipinas sits a walk from Chase Center, and Daly City, Chinatown and San Jose's Little Saigon are fan-base anchors. The Bay also invented Filipino-American battle turntablism (Invisibl Skratch Piklz).
topInsights.implication: Show up now with paid, credited work and no merchandise during Filipino American History Month, sign a Chinatown-rooted artist by early November for a small Year of the Goat capsule (Feb 6, 2027), and be open that the full Filipino capsule is an October 2027 build. No generic dragons or 'chop suey' type.

topInsights.title: Underdog anniversaries and the team-first story beat dynasty hype
topInsights.insight: We Believe turns 20 in spring 2027 and shares a soundtrack with hyphy (E-40's 2006 breakout), while Bay vintage dealers and the Alameda Point flea already trade Run TMC, We Believe and Oakland-era gear that fans buy before the current jersey. 'Strength in Numbers' fits a roster with few new stars better than star-led gear.
topInsights.implication: Treat heritage as the hero category with numbered, story-led pieces priced as collector items, and use Strength in Numbers as the through-line for team-first product so new gear isn't compared with cheap vintage or tied to one injured player.

collection.name: Both Sides of the Bridge
collection.story: The logo shows the Bay Bridge, which opened Nov 12, 1936, and Chase Center sits a short walk from it, so the Warriors' own mark is a span between The City and The Town. This collection gives The Town, The City and the 408 their own voices, made by named local letterers, builders and artists, and cuts every piece for a fog-and-rain season; winter 2026 pilots it, and 2027-28 builds it out.

risks.risk: Cultural lifting: hyphy slang, scraper-bike style and lowrider pinstripes come from Black Oakland and Chicano communities, and only some partners are signed.
risks.mitigation: Develop nothing from a community without a named, paid partner from it holding approval rights; the lowrider half stays on hold until a Chicano-led club or painter signs.

risks.risk: A licensing thicket: Golden Gate Bridge district, The Bay Lights, SFMTA's Muni worm, Fillmore and Grateful Dead archive art, Hieroglyphics and Thizz marks, We Believe and Oracle audio, and mural copyright.
risks.mitigation: Commission original art from living Bay artists, draw bridges from public geometry, and clear every third-party and pre-Oakland mark with the team and NBA before sampling.

scorecard.rationale: Oakland, San Francisco and Asian American lineages put the Bay's design well in the league's top band and its spending keeps retail high, but a 40.5-win total and an open Curry shoe deal hold opportunity and fandom at the league middle (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 70). Culture is near the top (two cities, three subcultural lineages, huge Asian American communities), but opportunity is held to the low 70s by a 40.5 win total, injured Butler and Moody, an open Curry deal and a winter-only window. A Curry-Nike deal, confirmed Specter game dates and a hot November would move it back toward 80.

music.headline: The Bay invented its own sound three times (Fillmore psychedelia, Vallejo-Oakland hyphy, Filipino-American battle turntablism), and the Warriors' music credibility still lives across the bridge in The Town.
music.summary: Bay Area music has three homegrown movements a designer can draw on: 1960s psychedelic rock and the Fillmore poster art that came with it in San Francisco, the 'go dumb' hyphy movement of mid-2000s Vallejo and Oakland, and the turntablism that Filipino-American DJ crews built in Daly City and the Excelsior. The rap canon fans rep is overwhelmingly East Bay (Too $hort, Digital Underground, Hieroglyphics, Mac Dre, Keak da Sneak, E-40). The Warriors' own music ties grew up at Oracle Arena in Oakland and are carried today by courtside fixtures E-40 and MC Hammer and by longtime in-arena DJ D-Sharp. After a 37-45 season, with an aging Curry core running it back, music-led product can keep Dub Nation invested even if the standings don't. Build it with Oakland and Vallejo artists, Bay poster makers and Filipino-American DJs, launch it in their rooms, and license or skip every iconic asset.

insights.title: Hyphy and 'We Believe' are one memory
insights.detail: Hyphy, the hyperactive rap and dance movement built by Mac Dre, Keak da Sneak, Mistah F.A.B. and E-40, broke nationally with E-40's 'Tell Me When to Go' in 2006. That is the same window in which the 2007 'We Believe' Warriors, an 8 seed, knocked off 67-win Dallas in front of a roaring Oracle crowd.
insights.implication: For fans now in their 30s and 40s, hyphy's language and look are the soundtrack of their Warriors. That makes them the native vocabulary for an Oakland-heritage capsule, which should be built with Vallejo and Oakland artists rather than from a mood board.

insights.title: E-40 is Dub Nation's most visible celebrity fan
insights.detail: The Vallejo rapper has sat courtside since the Oracle years. When he was escorted out of Sacramento's Golden 1 Center during the 2023 Warriors-Kings playoff series, he called it racial profiling and the Bay rallied behind him.
insights.implication: He is the most credible bridge between the team and Bay rap, but he runs his own wine and spirits businesses (Earl Stevens Selections, Sluricane). Approach him as a paid co-creator with clear category boundaries, never as a cameo.

insights.title: The arena sound has a name: DJ D-Sharp
insights.detail: DJ D-Sharp, the Warriors' longtime in-arena DJ, carried the team's mix of Bay slaps and anthems from Oracle Arena to Chase Center. For many fans the in-game sound is his.
insights.implication: Make him the paid music curator for city drops. A licensed D-Sharp warmup mix as launch content gives product Bay credibility that a brand team cannot manufacture.

insights.title: Fillmore poster art is San Francisco's native graphic language
insights.detail: From 1966, Bill Graham's Fillmore posters by Wes Wilson, Victor Moscoso, Stanley Mouse and Alton Kelley, and Rick Griffin defined psychedelic design: hand-drawn letters swelling to fill a shape, and complementary colors that vibrate. The Fillmore still hands sold-out crowds a free commemorative poster, and the Warriors have kept the Haight connection alive with recurring Grateful Dead nights.
insights.implication: A numbered game-poster series drawn by living Bay poster artists is the most 'only San Francisco' visual a Warriors product can carry. Commission new work, and license archive art from its rights holders instead of tracing the classics.

insights.title: Battle turntablism is Bay-born and Filipino-American
insights.detail: Filipino-American mobile DJ crews in Daly City, San Francisco's Excelsior and the East Bay produced the Invisibl Skratch Piklz (DJ Qbert, Mix Master Mike, Shortkut), whose members won DMC world titles in the early 1990s and turned the turntable into an instrument. Pinole's P-Lo carries that lineage into today's rap production.
insights.implication: Turntable, slipmat and scratch-waveform graphics are earned Bay motifs and a natural story for Filipino American History Month in October and the Warriors' Filipino Heritage Night. Co-design the work with Filipino-American DJs, and credit and pay them.

insights.title: Oakland made the music; San Francisco has the address
insights.detail: Chase Center opened in Mission Bay in September 2019 with Metallica and the San Francisco Symphony, ending 47 years in Oakland, the city that produced most of the Bay rap canon. Many 'Town' fans, who also lost the Raiders and A's, still feel the move.
insights.implication: Music-led product should carry both 'The Town' and 'The City' and launch in Oakland rooms such as the Fox Theater. Product that only speaks Chase Center reads as tech-money San Francisco to the fan base's emotional core.

places.name: The Fillmore
places.why: Bill Graham's rock room since 1966, in the old 'Harlem of the West' jazz district, and still the place that gives sold-out crowds a free commemorative poster.

places.name: Fox Theater
places.why: A restored 1928 movie palace where Bay rap and R&B acts play their homecoming shows, which makes it the right Oakland stage for a Town product launch.

places.name: Oakland Arena (formerly Oracle Arena)
places.why: The 'Roaracle,' the Warriors' home for 47 years and the building where 'We Believe' happened; it still hosts concerts and remains a pilgrimage point for Oakland fans.

places.name: Chase Center and Thrive City
places.why: The current home court, opened in 2019 with Metallica and the SF Symphony; Thrive City's plaza is the natural stage for DJ-led launches on game days.

places.name: 924 Gilman Street
places.why: An all-ages, volunteer-run punk club since 1986 that launched Green Day, Operation Ivy and Rancid: the East Bay's DIY conscience.

places.name: Amoeba Music
places.why: The Bay's flagship record store, in a former bowling alley a few blocks from the Grateful Dead's old house, and the right door for a numbered poster-tee drop.

places.name: SFJAZZ Center
places.why: Billed as the first free-standing U.S. building made for jazz (2013), it carries forward the Fillmore jazz legacy that urban renewal destroyed.

places.name: KPOO 89.5 FM
places.why: A noncommercial community station on air since 1972, playing blues, jazz, gospel and hip-hop for Black San Francisco: a partner with deep roots, not reach.

places.name: 106 KMEL
places.why: For decades the Bay's hip-hop and R&B station and the dial where Bay rap and hyphy broke to a mass audience.

places.name: Sigmund Stern Grove
places.why: A eucalyptus-ringed natural amphitheater that has hosted free Sunday summer concerts since 1938, beloved across every Bay demographic.

people.name: E-40
people.role: Vallejo rapper, slang coiner and entrepreneur
people.why: The Warriors' most visible celebrity fan and an architect of mobb music and hyphy, with the authority to bless or sink a Bay music collab.

people.name: DJ D-Sharp
people.why: He has soundtracked games from Oracle to Chase Center, so he is the team's built-in music curator.

people.name: MC Hammer
people.role: East Oakland pop-rap superstar and former A's batboy
people.why: A courtside regular through the title years and a living symbol of Oakland's claim on the team.

people.name: Larry June
people.role: San Francisco rapper and independent label owner (The Freeminded Records)
people.why: His wellness-and-vintage-cars persona and his 2023 album with The Alchemist, 'The Great Escape,' make him the city's most respected current voice.

people.name: LaRussell
people.role: Vallejo rapper and independent operator (Good Compenny)
people.why: His backyard shows and fast, fan-owned release model are the new template for Bay independence; he is a natural co-creator if he has no conflicting deals.

people.name: P-Lo
people.role: Filipino-American rapper-producer from Pinole; HBK Gang member
people.why: He links the Bay's Filipino-American DJ lineage to current rap and is a credible voice for Filipino Heritage Night.

people.name: DJ Qbert
people.role: San Francisco turntablist; co-founder of the Invisibl Skratch Piklz
people.why: A DMC world champion and the global face of Bay turntablism, still teaching scratching worldwide.

people.name: Hieroglyphics
people.role: Oakland indie hip-hop collective (Del the Funky Homosapien, Souls of Mischief, Casual, Pep Love, Domino)
people.why: Behind '93 'til Infinity' and the Hiero Day festival, and holders of the third-eye logo, one of hip-hop's best-known collective marks.

moments.name: Carnaval San Francisco
moments.why: The Mission's Latin American and Caribbean music, dance and parade weekend, rooted in the neighborhood that raised Carlos Santana.

moments.name: Fillmore Jazz Festival
moments.why: A free street festival on Fillmore Street that honors the 'Harlem of the West' and fits naturally with a Fillmore poster-art story.

moments.name: Stern Grove Festival
moments.why: Free summer concerts with an all-ages crowd in the Sunset, an off-season way to keep the brand in front of families.

moments.name: Outside Lands
moments.why: The Bay's biggest ticketed festival and the summer's peak reach for previewing next season's city product.

moments.name: San Jose Jazz Summer Fest
moments.why: The South Bay's signature music weekend, a way into the Silicon Valley fan base that rarely sees Bay culture activations.

moments.name: Hiero Day
moments.why: Hieroglyphics' Oakland block-party festival is the pre-season gathering of East Bay hip-hop heads and an ideal seeding moment for a Town capsule.

moments.name: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass
moments.why: Warren Hellman's free Golden Gate Park festival, which draws hundreds of thousands just as preseason starts.

moments.name: Filipino American History Month and Warriors Filipino Heritage Night
moments.timing: October (heritage night date set each season)
moments.why: The best moment for a turntablism story co-created with Filipino-American DJs, in one of the country's largest Filipino-American communities.

vocabulary.meaning: Short for hyperactive: the mid-2000s Bay rap, dance and car-culture movement out of Vallejo and Oakland.
To lose yourself dancing, the core hyphy instruction, immortalized by E-40's 'Tell Me When to Go.'
The slow, funk-heavy, bass-driven 1990s Bay rap sound of Vallejo and Oakland (E-40 and The Click, Spice 1, Mac Mall).
Bay slang for a song that hits hard, rooted in trunk-rattling Bay beats and now used nationally.
Oakland and San Francisco respectively; every Bay music fan knows which side an artist reps.
The Bay Area ('Yay Area'), a common term in Bay rap lyrics.
The quintessential Northern California intensifier ('hella loud'), worn as a badge of Bay identity.
Mac Dre's term (and his Thizz Entertainment label), which refers to ecstasy. Know it, but keep it off product.

designCues.cue: Fillmore melt: hand-drawn letterforms that swell and warp to fill a shape
designCues.source: Wes Wilson's 1966-67 Fillmore posters, which set the template for psychedelic lettering.
designCues.use: Commission Bay letterers to draw 'Dub Nation' or 'The Bay' in this tradition for poster tees and hangtags. Do not copy or trace existing posters.

designCues.cue: Vibration orange set against Warriors Royal
designCues.source: Victor Moscoso's Fillmore-era optical clashes of equal-value complementary colors.
designCues.use: Use it as the single hit color against Warriors Royal (#1D428A) on poster prints, taping or an inside placket, tuned so the two vibrate. The hex is approximate, so match it with a lab dip.

designCues.cue: Scraper-bike candy foil: spokes wrapped in candy wrappers and colored foil tape
designCues.source: East Oakland's scraper-bike youth culture, put on the map by the Trunk Boiz' 2007 'Scraper Bike' video and the Original Scraper Bike Team.
designCues.use: Use iridescent foil-tape piping, spoke-pattern heat transfers and candy-color colorblocking, co-created with East Oakland scraper builders who are credited and paid.

designCues.cue: Stunna shades: oversized white-frame sunglasses
designCues.source: The signature accessory of the hyphy era (Mac Dre, Keak da Sneak, E-40's 'Tell Me When to Go' video).
designCues.use: Use as a graphic icon or campaign styling for an Oakland-heritage capsule, paired with 'Go Dumb' type, never with 'Thizz' imagery.

designCues.cue: Turntable, slipmat and scratch waveform
designCues.source: Bay turntablism built by Filipino-American DJ crews and the Invisibl Skratch Piklz.
designCues.use: Print the waveform of a commissioned scratch routine by a named Bay DJ down a sleeve, cut slipmat-shaped hangtags, and credit the DJ on the tag.

designCues.cue: The Roaracle: crowd noise as heritage
designCues.source: Oracle Arena's reputation as the league's loudest building, peaking with the 2007 'We Believe' run.
designCues.use: Build a Town capsule around decibel-meter graphics and a waveform from licensed Oracle crowd audio in the team archive, and launch it in Oakland.

designCues.cue: Two decks, one bridge
designCues.source: The Bay Bridge in the Warriors logo combined with the Bay's DJ culture.
designCues.use: Redraw the bridge as the line between two turntables labeled The Town and The City, as the chest graphic for a capsule that unites Oakland and San Francisco. The logo is team IP and requires NBA/team approval.

productHooks: A 'Go Dumb' Oakland-heritage capsule (shooting shirt, hoodie, crew socks) with scraper-foil piping and stunna-shade graphics, co-designed with Vallejo and Oakland artists such as LaRussell, launched at a Fox Theater show, with proceeds to an East Oakland youth music or bike program.

Numbered Fillmore-style poster tees for marquee nights (Oct. 21 at the Lakers, Dec. 25 vs. Denver), each drawn by a commissioned Bay poster artist and sold with a printed poster at Amoeba Haight and the Chase Center team store.

A turntablism capsule for October's Filipino American History Month and the Warriors' Filipino Heritage Night, with scratch-waveform sleeves and slipmat hangtags, co-created with Bay Filipino-American DJs (approach DJ Qbert or P-Lo) and launched with a Thrive City DJ set.
A DJ D-Sharp warmup tee for the home opener, carrying a QR code to a licensed D-Sharp Bay mix, sold at Thrive City.
A 'Roaracle' Town tee with a waveform of the 2007 'We Believe' crowd noise, sold in Oakland stores and at a Hiero Day or Oakland pop-up rather than only at Chase Center.
watchouts: Brand conflicts: Stephen Curry ended his Under Armour partnership in late 2025 (Curry Brand is independent) and his next partner is unconfirmed. Use him only through NBA-licensed assets in music content, and check every artist's apparel and beverage deals (E-40's spirits businesses included) before approaching them.

Third-party IP: Fillmore and Bill Graham archive posters, Grateful Dead marks (Steal Your Face, dancing bears), Hieroglyphics' third-eye logo, Thizz Entertainment marks, KMEL marks, and all song titles, lyrics and audio require licenses. Commission new art instead of tracing classics.

Hyphy-era imagery carries drug and danger references ('thizz,' ghost-riding, sideshows), and Oakland is actively cracking down on sideshows. Keep product to music, dance, stunna shades and scraper bikes.
Oakland's loss is real: the Warriors, Raiders and A's all left, so Oakland-nostalgia product without Oakland artists, Oakland launch venues and money back into Oakland will read as exploitation.

Filipino-American turntablism, Black Fillmore jazz history and Mission Latino music each belong to specific communities. Partner with them, credit them and pay them, and do not reduce any of them to a costume or a single stereotype.

verify: DJ D-Sharp is still the Warriors' in-arena DJ at Chase Center for 2026-27.

Stephen Curry's current footwear and apparel partner (left Under Armour late 2025), and any apparel or beverage deals held by E-40, Larry June, LaRussell, P-Lo or DJ Qbert, before anyone is approached.
2026-27 Warriors promo calendar: home opener date, Filipino Heritage Night date, and whether a Grateful Dead night returns (and how any tribute is handled).
E-40 and MC Hammer remain regular courtside presences at Chase Center.
The 2026-27 City Edition design (not yet verified), so music capsules complement rather than clash with the on-court look.
Oakland Arena is still booking concerts under the Coliseum site's new ownership.
Whether Hiero Day ran in Oakland on Labor Day 2026 and its 2027 plans.
2026-27 festival dates: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass (early October 2026), Carnaval SF, Stern Grove, Fillmore Jazz Festival, Outside Lands and San Jose Jazz Summer Fest 2027.
The Fillmore still gives free posters at sold-out shows, and who currently licenses the Bill Graham poster archive.
The Original Scraper Bike Team is still active in East Oakland and open to a paid collaboration.
106 KMEL still runs a hip-hop/R&B format and KPOO 89.5 is still broadcasting.
Larry June's and LaRussell's current labels and activity, and that the Fox Theater, 924 Gilman, Amoeba Haight and SFJAZZ Center are operating as described.

art.headline: The Warriors' visual world is a two-city argument painted on walls: Mission murals and Fillmore poster lettering in The City, Panther-era print graphics and candy-paint scrapers in The Town, joined by the Bay Bridge in the team's own logo, not the Golden Gate on every souvenir tee.
art.summary: Bay Area visual culture is collaborative and political: Balmy Alley (early 1970s), Precita Eyes (1977) and Clarion Alley (1992) made the Mission one of America's densest mural districts, and many of those walls argue against the tech wealth that now fills Chase Center. San Francisco's typographic exports, from Wes Wilson's Fillmore poster lettering and the Mission School's sign-painter letters to Walter Landor's 1975 Muni worm and Timothy Pflueger's deco theater signs, sit beside Oakland's own: Emory Douglas's Black Panther graphics, Lake Merritt's Necklace of Lights, and a car culture of candy-paint scrapers and scraper bikes that runs south to San Jose, where Lowrider Magazine started in 1977. Because the team left Oakland for Mission Bay in 2019 after 47 seasons, every cue has to answer which side of the bridge it serves, and the logo already gives the answer: the Bay Bridge that joins both. Nike's opening is to commission from this bench of muralists, poster artists, Oakland printmakers and car-culture builders instead of defaulting to Golden Gate orange and 'Hella' souvenir type.

insights.title: The logo already picked the bridge
insights.detail: Since 2010 the Warriors' roundel has shown the Bay Bridge, which joins The City to The Town; the Golden Gate is the tourist bridge and leads to Marin. The team played 47 seasons in Oakland (1971-2019, minus 1996-97 in San Jose) before moving to Chase Center.
insights.implication: Make Bay Bridge cable lines and paired City/Town graphics the spine of any Warriors art program; treat Golden Gate orange as an accent at most, and give Oakland equal billing and equal commissions.

insights.title: The Town lost its teams but kept its look
insights.detail: Oakland lost the Warriors (2019), the Raiders (2020) and the A's (after 2024), and its civic identity now lives in Oaklandish's oak-tree tees, Uptown and KONO murals, and First Fridays on Telegraph Avenue.
insights.implication: Oakland-facing product has to be co-authored with Oakland artists and sold through Oakland doors; a 'The Town' graphic without an Oakland maker's name on it will read as the team cashing in on a place it left.

insights.title: Mission murals are community property with a point of view
insights.detail: Balmy Alley's garage-door murals, Precita Eyes' youth and tour programs, the Women's Building's MaestraPeace (1994) and Clarion Alley's rotating walls are collectively made, and Clarion's recent work often targets tech-driven displacement, the same money that sits courtside at Chase Center.
insights.implication: Commission and pay Mission muralists through Precita Eyes; never use these walls as a campaign backdrop or print photographed murals, which are the artists' copyright.

insights.title: San Francisco exported its own letterforms
insights.detail: Wes Wilson's 1966-67 Fillmore posters invented the swelling, shape-filling psychedelic letter, and the Fillmore still hands posters to fans at sold-out shows; Landor's continuous-line Muni worm and Margaret Kilgallen's and Barry McGee's sign-painter lettering are equally local.
insights.implication: Draw Warriors wordmarks in these traditions, commissioned as originals from living Bay letterers and poster artists, instead of using stock script; license the Muni worm from SFMTA if it appears.

insights.title: Oakland is a print-and-poster city
insights.detail: Emory Douglas's graphics for The Black Panther newspaper (bold outlines, flat color, woodcut hatching), Favianna Rodriguez's screenprints and Creative Growth's studio of artists with disabilities (since 1974) make Oakland's art political, graphic and print-native.
insights.implication: Build February and community product on screenprint texture and Oakland printmakers, with credit and pay; Creative Growth is a strong candidate for an inclusive, artist-credited capsule.

insights.title: Car culture is the shared East Bay and South Bay language
insights.detail: Oakland's 'scrapers' (big-rim GM sedans in candy paint), East Oakland's Scraper Bike Team with its foil-wrapped spokes, and San Jose's lowrider scene, where Lowrider Magazine was founded in 1977, share candy paint, metal flake and pinstriping.
insights.implication: Candy-paint finishes and pinstripe details can link Oakland and San Jose fans in one capsule, made with named builders; celebrate the craft, never the illegal sideshows.

insights.title: The arena's neighbors are galleries
insights.detail: Chase Center in Mission Bay sits a short walk from Dogpatch's Minnesota Street Project (2016) and ICA San Francisco (2022), with the Bayview and Hunters Point Shipyard studios just beyond.
insights.implication: Stage artist reveals and limited art drops in Dogpatch on game nights so the art program lives in the arena's own neighborhood rather than only inside the team store.

places.name: Balmy Alley
places.neighborhood: Mission (24th to 25th St, between Treat Ave and Harrison St)
places.why: Murals since the early 1970s, including the 1984 PLACA project on Central America, make it the root of the Mission's community mural tradition.

places.name: Precita Eyes Mural Arts & Visitors Center
places.why: Founded in 1977 by Susan Kelk Cervantes and Luis Cervantes, it runs mural tours and youth programs and is the most credible door to commissioning Mission muralists.

places.name: Clarion Alley Mural Project
places.neighborhood: Mission (between Mission and Valencia, 17th and 18th Streets)
places.why: A rotating, artist-curated alley since 1992 whose murals take on housing, policing and tech displacement; it shows what the Mission is saying right now.

places.name: Minnesota Street Project
places.why: Opened in 2016 as a cluster of galleries and artist studios a short walk south of Chase Center, with ICA San Francisco (2022) on the same street.

places.name: African American Art & Culture Complex
places.why: The long-running home for Black visual and performing artists in a neighborhood once called the Harlem of the West, and a natural partner for San Francisco Black History product.

places.name: The Fillmore
places.neighborhood: Western Addition (Geary Blvd at Fillmore St)
places.why: Its hallways of concert posters and its poster handout at sold-out shows keep San Francisco's psychedelic lettering tradition alive.

places.name: Oakland Museum of California
places.why: Oakland's civic museum of California art and history, which has staged major shows on the Black Panthers and on Bay Area art and design.

places.name: Creative Growth Art Center
places.kind: art studio and gallery for artists with disabilities
places.why: Since 1974 it has run a working studio and gallery for artists with disabilities, a model for credited, paid and inclusive collaboration.

places.name: MACLA (Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana)
places.neighborhood: SoFA District, downtown San Jose (S. First St)
places.why: San Jose's main Latino contemporary art space and the right door to South Bay Chicano and lowrider-rooted artists.

places.name: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco
places.why: Runs contemporary exhibitions and Chinatown art programs, so it is the place to find Chinese American artists for Lunar New Year work instead of using stock Chinatown imagery.

people.name: Emory Douglas
people.role: Graphic artist; Minister of Culture of the Black Panther Party
people.why: A San Francisco-raised artist whose Black Panther newspaper graphics defined Oakland's political visual language; a commission or tribute made with him carries real weight in The Town.

people.name: Precita Eyes Muralists (Susan Kelk Cervantes)
people.role: Mural collective and nonprofit; Cervantes is founder and a MaestraPeace co-painter
people.why: Has trained and organized generations of Mission muralists and is the community-accountable way to commission murals or mural-based product.

people.name: Barry McGee
people.role: Painter and graffiti writer (Twist); Mission School
people.why: The best-known figure in San Francisco's street-to-gallery lineage, with deep skateboard and streetwear credibility; a top-tier collaborator who needs a top-tier brief.

people.name: Favianna Rodriguez
people.role: Oakland-born printmaker and cultural organizer (Center for Cultural Power)
people.why: Her bold screenprints, including the 'Migration Is Beautiful' monarch, are Oakland's best-known Latina graphic voice and a credible partner for Latino heritage product.

people.name: Jeremy Fish
people.why: His San Francisco-centric drawings have run through skate and streetwear graphics for two decades, including with Haight Street's Upper Playground, which makes him a natural fit for a City-side capsule.

people.name: Scraper Bike Team (Tyrone 'Baybe Champ' Stevenson Jr.)
people.why: Turned Oakland's scraper car style into candy-colored, foil-spoked bikes and a youth program; the most authentic partner for a car-culture capsule.

people.name: Oaklandish
people.why: Started in 2000 as a public art project and became The Town's civic uniform; the benchmark, and a possible partner, for Oakland-pride product.

people.name: FTC Skateboarding
people.why: Its multiple Nike SB Dunk collaborations make it San Francisco's most direct sneaker-culture link to Nike.

moments.name: FOG Design+Art
moments.why: The fair that benefits SFMOMA gathers the city's collectors and design crowd, the same audience as Chase Center's premium seats, making it the venue for a high-end artist collaboration reveal.

moments.name: San Francisco Chinese New Year Festival & Parade
moments.timing: Lunar New Year is Feb 6, 2027 (Year of the Goat); the Chinatown night parade usually follows within about two weeks
moments.why: One of the largest Lunar New Year parades outside Asia, led by its long golden dragon, and the anchor for the Warriors' big Chinese American and Asian American fan base.

moments.name: Black Joy Parade
moments.why: Oakland's homegrown Black History Month celebration of color, costume and joy, and the right stage for Oakland Black artists' product.

moments.name: Oakland First Fridays
moments.timing: First Friday of every month, Telegraph Ave (KONO)
moments.why: The Town's monthly street festival of artists and vendors, which grew out of the Art Murmur gallery walks; a standing place to scout and launch Oakland work.

moments.name: Fillmore sold-out show poster handout
moments.why: The ritual that keeps San Francisco poster art collectible, and a ready model for numbered game-night prints.

moments.name: Carnaval San Francisco
moments.why: The Mission's biggest costume and parade design moment, held during the 2027 playoff window.

moments.name: San Francisco Open Studios (ArtSpan)
moments.timing: Weekends from mid-October into November, neighborhood by neighborhood
moments.why: A citywide open-studios circuit that has run for decades and lines up with tip-off, making it the most efficient way to scout and sign City-side collaborators.

moments.name: Día de los Muertos procession and Festival of Altars
moments.timing: Nov 2 at dusk, Mission (altars in Garfield Square)
moments.why: A living community ritual since the early 1980s, where Mission artists build altars; a place to meet and listen to artists, not a merchandise moment.

vocabulary.meaning: Oakland, said with pride; past Warriors uniforms have used it as an Oakland tribute.
San Francisco, and the wordmark on the 1960s San Francisco Warriors jersey; locals never call it 'Frisco' or 'San Fran'.
Bay Area rap's name for the whole region, a credible alternative to 'The Bay' on graphics.
The Bay-born intensifier ('hella cold'); authentic but now a souvenir-shop staple, so use it sparingly and only in a local artist's hand.
Warriors fandom; 'the Dubs' is the team's everyday nickname.
Oakland and East Bay term for a 1970s-80s GM sedan on big rims in candy paint, and the root of East Oakland's scraper bikes.
The 1990s San Francisco art movement of Barry McGee, Margaret Kilgallen, Chris Johanson and Alicia McCarthy, built on graffiti, folk art and hand-painted signs.
The nickname locals give San Francisco's summer fog, which has its own social-media persona; shorthand for the city's cold, gray weather.

designCues.cue: Bay Bridge cable geometry: the suspension span's long catenaries and vertical hangers, with a dot-matrix run of white light points down the cables.
designCues.source: The Bay Bridge in the Warriors' logo since 2010, and Leo Villareal's The Bay Lights (2013) on the West Span's cables.
designCues.use: Catenary line graphics on side panels and shorts with reflective dot-matrix prints; any direct Bay Lights reference needs a license from the artist and Illuminate.

designCues.cue: Candy royal: Warriors royal #1D428A laid over silver metal flake as a candy-paint finish, with Warriors gold #FFC72C hand pinstriping.
designCues.source: Oakland scrapers, East Oakland's foil-spoked scraper bikes and San Jose lowriders.
designCues.use: Metal-flake prints, high-gloss trims and pinstripe details, co-designed with and credited to named Bay car-culture builders.

designCues.cue: Fillmore poster lettering: letters that swell and bend to fill a shape, in vibrating complementary color pairs.
designCues.source: Wes Wilson's 1966-67 Fillmore posters, which drew on Vienna Secession lettering, and the Bay's living gig-poster scene.
designCues.use: Commission a living Bay poster artist to draw an original 'DUBS' or 'THE CITY' lockup; never trace Wilson, Victor Moscoso or Grateful Dead artwork.

designCues.cue: Two-city deco: tall, narrow Art Deco capitals stacked vertically like theater blade signs, with a neon edge glow.
designCues.source: Timothy Pflueger's Castro Theatre (San Francisco, 1922) and Paramount Theatre (Oakland, 1931), plus the Fox Oakland and Grand Lake marquees.
designCues.use: Stack 'THE CITY' and 'THE TOWN' down opposite side seams of one garment; have a local sign painter draw an original alphabet rather than copying any one sign.

designCues.cue: Panther-press graphics: heavy black outlines, flat color fields and woodcut-style hatching, with people drawn at heroic scale.
designCues.source: Emory Douglas's art for The Black Panther newspaper, published in Oakland from 1967.
designCues.use: Screenprint-textured February product commissioned from Douglas or Oakland printmakers; no weapons, no 'pig' caricatures and no reuse of archival Panther art without the artist and rights holders.

designCues.cue: Karl gray: the cool, slightly blue gray of fog pouring over Twin Peaks (approx. #C4C8CA).
designCues.source: San Francisco's summer fog, nicknamed Karl, which makes layering the local uniform.
designCues.use: A heather base for fleece and layering pieces with Warriors gold as the only accent, a quiet City-side alternative to Golden Gate orange.

designCues.cue: Alley panel quilt: one garment built from separately authored panels, each a different muralist's story, like Balmy Alley's garage doors.
designCues.source: Balmy Alley, painted since the early 1970s, including the 1984 PLACA project.
designCues.use: A multi-artist warm-up jacket or shooting shirt with each panel credited on the jock tag, commissioned through Precita Eyes; never print photographs of existing murals.

designCues.cue: Necklace of Lights: a scalloped string of round bulbs looping the water and doubled in its reflection.
designCues.source: Lake Merritt's lights, first strung in 1925 and later restored, around the lake where Oakland gathers.
designCues.use: A scalloped bulb-chain trim or all-over print for Oakland-facing product, sold through Oakland shops.

productHooks: 'The City / The Town' capsule: fog-gray heather base, Bay Bridge catenary graphics, and Pflueger-style blade lettering with 'THE CITY' down one seam and 'THE TOWN' down the other, drawn by one San Francisco and one Oakland letterer who are both credited and paid.

'Candy Paint' capsule: Warriors royal over metal flake with gold pinstriping and reflective foil-spoke trims, co-designed with the Scraper Bike Team and San Jose lowrider builders and launched in East Oakland and at MACLA.
Numbered game-night posters: a Bay poster artist draws a Fillmore-style screenprint for select marquee home games, handed to fans and sold with a matching tee, and the artist signs the run.

Oakland Black History capsule for February, timed to the Black Joy Parade: screenprint graphics commissioned from Emory Douglas or Oakland printmakers, sold through Oaklandish and Black-owned Oakland shops, with proceeds to an Oakland organization the artist chooses.
Mission panel jacket for the Warriors' Latino heritage night or Carnaval weekend, with each panel painted by a Precita Eyes muralist and credited on the jock tag.

Lunar New Year 2027 (Year of the Goat) capsule drawn by Chinatown-rooted artists found through the Chinese Culture Center, using neon blade-sign characters by a local calligrapher, not 'chop suey' type.
watchouts: Third-party IP is everywhere: the Golden Gate Bridge district licenses the bridge's name and image, The Bay Lights is Leo Villareal's artwork, the Muni worm belongs to SFMTA, Grateful Dead and classic Fillmore poster art need licenses, and Oaklandish owns its tree logo. Murals are protected by copyright and California's Art Preservation Act.

Oakland is still sore about the 2019 move and lost the Raiders and A's too. Oakland cues need Oakland artists, Oakland retail and visible credit, or they read as nostalgia merch from the team that left.
Clarion Alley and many Mission murals protest tech-driven displacement. Using them as a backdrop for a brand shoot would be tone-deaf, so go through Precita Eyes and the artists themselves.

Avoid caricature: no 'chop suey' fonts or generic dragons for Chinatown, no Panther guns, no sugar-skull merchandise from Día de los Muertos, and no Old English or placa lettering lifted from Chicano street culture without Chicano artists. Celebrate scrapers and lowriders, never sideshows.

Stephen Curry ended his Under Armour partnership in late 2025 (Curry Brand now independent) and is reportedly a sneaker free agent; confirm his current footwear and apparel deal before commissioning any artist portrait of him for Nike product, and lean on team and city art rather than player likeness.

verify: The Warriors' City Edition history (including past Oakland 'The Town' tributes) and what the 2026-27 City Edition and Specter uniforms use, so these concepts don't duplicate them.
Stephen Curry's current footwear and apparel deal (he left Under Armour in late 2025; a new partner is unconfirmed) before any portrait-based product.
Dates of the Warriors' 2026-27 Lunar New Year, Black History and Latino heritage nights, and the 2027 San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade (Lunar New Year is Feb 6, 2027).
Black Joy Parade 2027 date and Oakland First Fridays' current schedule and format on Telegraph Ave.
San Francisco Open Studios 2026 weekends (ArtSpan) and FOG Design+Art January 2027 dates.
Carnaval San Francisco 2027 dates (expected Memorial Day weekend, May 29-30).
That FTC Skateboarding, Upper Playground and Oaklandish are still operating, and where their stores are.
Scraper Bike Team's current activity and leadership.
Whether The Bay Lights is currently lit (the original installation went dark in 2023) and who licenses it.
Current Golden Gate Bridge district licensing rules for the bridge's name and image, and SFMTA licensing for the Muni worm.
Clarion Alley's current murals and CAMP's position on commercial photo shoots.
That the Fillmore still hands out commemorative posters at sold-out shows.

food.headline: Chase Center sits where the Bay's food lines cross: the T line runs from Chinatown past the arena into Black Bayview, 16th Street leads to the Mission's foil-wrapped burritos, Oakland barbecue is across the bridge, and the season runs straight through Dungeness crab season.
food.summary: The Bay Area's food identity passes any swap test: sourdough whose signature bacterium is named for San Francisco, the Dutch crunch roll, the foil-wrapped Mission burrito, Thanh Long's garlic noodles and roast crab, and a holiday table built on Dungeness crab and North Beach cioppino. Its living edge is immigrant and community kitchens: Chinatown's Mister Jiu's, Filipino Daly City and ube, Vietnamese San Jose, the Fruitvale taco trucks and Black-owned Oakland barbecue like Everett & Jones. Game day runs through Thrive City and the T Third line, and the Christmas-night home game against Denver lands in peak crab season. The Curry family made food part of the franchise's public face, but athlete ventures and the small businesses whose names locals actually wear are separate IP to license and pay. Nike's opening is table textures and colors (Dutch crunch crackle, crab orange, ube, burrito foil) co-created with the businesses that own them, and sold in Oakland as well as at Chase Center.

insights.title: Chase Center sits on a food line
insights.detail: Since the Central Subway opened in late 2022, the T Third light rail has run from Chinatown–Rose Pak station past the UCSF/Chase Center stop and down Third Street into Bayview, the city's historically Black neighborhood. Meanwhile 16th Street runs from the arena door straight west to the Mission's taquerías, and Thrive City, the plaza wrapped around the arena, is the pregame meeting point and road-game watch-party site.
insights.implication: Plan game-day activations as a route, not a booth. Pay one Chinatown bakery and one Bayview kitchen for collab menu items, and drop product at Thrive City and at both ends of the line.

insights.title: Christmas night is crab night
insights.detail: Dungeness crab is the Bay's holiday meal. The commercial season traditionally opens in mid-November, though recent openers have been delayed by whale-entanglement and domoic-acid rules. Christmas Eve means cioppino, the stew North Beach's Ligurian fishermen created, and from January to March 'crab feeds' (all-you-can-eat fundraisers) fill parish halls and school gyms. The Warriors host Denver on Christmas night at 7:30 p.m. PT.
insights.implication: A Christmas-game holiday pack in cooked-crab orange on Warriors navy is pure Bay. Tie part of the proceeds to a community crab feed, and don't date-lock product to the crab opener.

insights.title: Bread is the Bay's texture library
insights.detail: Sourdough's key bacterium was named Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis for the city in 1971, Boudin traces its mother dough to 1849, and Tartine's scored country loaf set the modern standard. Dutch crunch, the crackle-topped roll, is the default sandwich bread at Bay delis and almost unknown outside Northern California.
insights.implication: Dutch crunch crackle and sourdough scoring are textures no other market owns. Use them as tonal embosses, jacquards or prints on warm-ups, with the bacterium story on an inside label.

insights.title: Oakland feeds the loyalty
insights.detail: Oakland, the team's home from 1971 to 2019, has its own table: Everett & Jones Barbeque (Black-owned since 1973), the taco trucks along International Boulevard through Fruitvale, Oakland Chinatown, Ethiopian and Eritrean kitchens on Telegraph, and chefs like Tanya Holland, Nelson German and Reem Assil. Many Oakland fans still cheer the team and still resent the move across the bay.
insights.implication: Give Oakland a drop of its own, co-created with Oakland food businesses and sold in Oakland, rather than a nostalgia graphic sold at Chase Center.

insights.title: Filipino, Vietnamese and Chinese kitchens are the fan base's comfort food
insights.detail: Daly City is roughly a third Filipino, and Mitchell's Ice Cream has served ube and buko since long before ube went national. San Jose has the largest Vietnamese population of any U.S. city (Lee's Sandwiches was founded there in 1983), and the An family's garlic noodles at Thanh Long, served since 1971, became a citywide classic. October is Filipino American History Month, and the Warriors hold an annual Filipino Heritage Night.
insights.implication: Heritage capsules (ube for Filipino Heritage Night, Lunar New Year and Tết in February) should be co-designed with Filipino-, Vietnamese- and Chinese-American Bay creatives and kitchens, who are credited and paid, not built from color swatches.

insights.title: The Mission burrito is the city's edible logo, and a displacement flashpoint
insights.detail: The foil-wrapped Mission-style burrito is San Francisco's most recognizable dish. La Taqueria, which FiveThirtyEight named America's best burrito in 2014 and which is a James Beard America's Classic, famously leaves out the rice. The 24th Street corridor became the Calle 24 Latino Cultural District in 2014 to protect Latino businesses from tech-boom displacement, and La Cocina in the Mission incubates immigrant women food entrepreneurs.
insights.implication: Burrito foil and hand-painted taquería lettering are strong cues only when Latino businesses and artists are paid partners. Work through Calle 24 or La Cocina, and never frame the burrito as tech-worker fuel.

insights.title: The Currys made food part of the franchise's face
insights.detail: Ayesha Curry built a food brand (the cookbooks The Seasoned Life and The Full Plate, Food Network's Ayesha's Home Kitchen, Sweet July). She and Stephen run the Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation, which funds child nutrition and food access in Oakland, Stephen launched Gentleman's Cut bourbon, and Jimmy Butler owns Bigface Coffee.
insights.implication: A food-access activation with Eat. Learn. Play. fits Dub Nation, but athlete ventures are separate IP bound up with endorsement deals. Check Curry's and Butler's current footwear and apparel contracts, and keep alcohol off youth product.

places.name: Thrive City
places.why: The plaza wrapped around Chase Center is the pregame meeting point and has hosted official watch parties for road playoff games, which makes it the obvious place for food-collab pop-ups.

places.name: La Taqueria
places.why: It serves the canonical Mission burrito, with no rice and an optional 'dorado' crisped tortilla, and is the reference point every burrito argument in the city starts from.

places.name: Thanh Long
places.why: The An family's roast Dungeness crab and garlic noodles, served since 1971, are the Bay's Vietnamese-American special-occasion meal.

places.name: Swan Oyster Depot
places.why: This counter-only seafood bar has been open since 1912, and its line for Dungeness crab, oysters and 'crab back' sums up the city's crab culture.

places.name: Mister Jiu's
places.why: Brandon Jew's Michelin-starred Chinese-American restaurant on Waverly Place is a short walk from the T line's Chinatown–Rose Pak terminus.

places.name: Old Skool Cafe
places.why: This jazz-era supper club is staffed by young people coming out of the justice and foster-care systems, in Bayview.

places.name: Everett & Jones Barbeque
places.why: Dorothy Everett and her family opened it in 1973; it is Oakland's Black-owned barbecue standard and an Oakland-first partner.

places.name: International Boulevard taco trucks
places.why: This is the Bay's densest run of taco trucks, panaderías and mariscos stands, the everyday food of Oakland's Mexican and Central American community.

places.name: Mitchell's Ice Cream
places.why: It has been open since 1953 and is famous for Filipino and tropical flavors (ube, buko, macapuno) that families drive in for from Daly City to Vallejo.

places.name: La Victoria Taqueria
places.why: Its cult orange sauce, sold by the bottle, is San Jose's edible signature and a late-night SJSU rite.

people.name: Ayesha Curry
people.role: Cookbook author, TV host, founder of Sweet July, co-founder with Stephen Curry of the Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation
people.why: She is the Bay food figure most closely tied to the team, and Eat. Learn. Play.'s Oakland food-access work is a credible, non-commercial partner for a Nike food activation.

people.name: Alice Waters
people.role: Founder of Chez Panisse (Berkeley, 1971) and the Edible Schoolyard
people.why: She defined 'California cuisine' (seasonal, local, farmers-market first), the Bay's food self-image that every chef here still answers to.

people.name: Brandon Jew
people.role: Chef-owner of Mister Jiu's; author of Mister Jiu's in Chinatown
people.why: He is the leading voice for modern Chinese-American cooking at the Chinatown end of the T line and a natural Lunar New Year partner.

people.name: Tanya Holland
people.role: Oakland chef, founder of Brown Sugar Kitchen, author of Tanya Holland's California Soul
people.why: She is Oakland's most prominent Black culinary voice, with a national platform through Top Chef and the James Beard Foundation.

people.name: Nelson German
people.role: Dominican-American Oakland chef (alaMar, Sobre Mesa; confirm both still operate); Top Chef contestant
people.why: His Afro-Latino Oakland cooking pairs naturally with Dominican-born Al Horford for a heritage collab.

people.name: Reem Assil
people.role: Palestinian-Syrian-American chef, founder of Reem's California, author of Arabiyya
people.why: She built an Arab street bakery in Oakland's Fruitvale around worker-centered values and is a key voice of the East Bay's immigrant food scene.

people.name: La Cocina
people.role: Mission District nonprofit incubator for low-income, mostly immigrant women food entrepreneurs (founded 2005)
people.why: It is the most credible pipeline to paid, credited collabs with immigrant-owned food businesses.

people.name: Señor Sisig
people.role: Filipino-Mexican food truck and restaurant brand founded in 2010 by Evan Kidera and Gil Payumo
people.why: Its sisig burritos and merch are Bay Filipino-American pride, which makes it a natural Filipino Heritage Night partner.

moments.name: Tip-off meets Filipino American History Month
moments.why: Filipino American History Month lines up with the start of the season, and the Warriors' Filipino Heritage Night is the natural launch for an ube capsule.

moments.name: Dungeness crab season opener
moments.why: The Bay's food calendar turns on it, with crab back on menus from Swan Oyster Depot to Thanh Long.

moments.name: Christmas night: Nuggets at Warriors
moments.why: The national nightcap comes from Chase Center the day after the Bay's Christmas Eve cioppino-and-crab tradition.

moments.name: Crab feed season
moments.why: All-you-can-eat Dungeness fundraisers run by schools, parishes and clubs are the Bay's most local winter ritual.

moments.name: Lunar New Year and Tết
moments.timing: Feb 6, 2027; SF Chinatown parade and San Jose Tết events follow
moments.why: San Francisco's Chinese New Year Parade is one of the largest outside Asia, and San Jose's Vietnamese community celebrates Tết on the same date.

moments.name: Black Joy Parade
moments.why: This Black History Month celebration brings Black-owned food vendors to downtown Oakland.

moments.name: Carnaval San Francisco
moments.why: The Mission's street festival of Latino and Caribbean food and music falls in the conference-finals window.

moments.name: Pregame at Thrive City
moments.why: Fans gather on the arena plaza before tip-off and come back for watch parties during road playoff runs.

vocabulary.meaning: A Mission-style burrito 'super'-sized with cheese, sour cream and guacamole; locals order it 'super' by default.
The crackle-topped sandwich roll standard at Bay delis and rare elsewhere; 'on Dutch crunch' is the local order.
An all-you-can-eat Dungeness crab fundraiser dinner held by schools, parishes and clubs in winter.
The Bay's word for bubble tea. A 'boba run' is a social ritual, especially for Asian-American youth.
Butter-and-garlic noodles popularized by Thanh Long and now on menus across the Bay, usually ordered with roast crab.
The Town is Oakland and The City is San Francisco. Call an Oakland food drop 'The City' and it fails.
A scramble of ground beef, spinach, onion and egg, a staple of the city's Italian-American 'Joe's' restaurants, including Original Joe's in North Beach and San Jose.
A sourdough starter kept alive for years. Boudin says its mother dough dates to 1849.

designCues.cue: Cooked Dungeness orange: the brick-orange of a boiled crab shell, paired with its shell-cream underside (#F3E3C3) on Warriors navy #1D428A
designCues.source: Dungeness crab season, Christmas Eve cioppino and winter crab feeds
designCues.use: Use it as a holiday-pack accent on collar tipping, number outlines and a bib-shaped hangtag, with no restaurant marks.

designCues.cue: Ube halaya purple, the deep violet of Filipino purple-yam jam, set against Warriors gold #FFC72C
designCues.source: Filipino-American desserts, from Daly City bakeries to Mitchell's ube ice cream
designCues.use: Use it for the Filipino Heritage Night colorway, co-designed with Filipino-American Bay designers. Keep the Philippine flag's sun and stars off unless partners lead.

designCues.cue: Dutch crunch crackle: the irregular cracked-plate pattern of the rice-paste topping, browned darker at the seams
designCues.source: The default sandwich roll at Bay delis
designCues.use: Use it as a tonal emboss on gold fleece or as a jacquard on warm-up sleeves, a texture no other market can claim.

designCues.cue: 'Named for the city': Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis, the sourdough bacterium, plus a single curved scoring 'ear' and a flour-dust bloom
designCues.source: San Francisco sourdough (Boudin since 1849, Tartine's country loaf)
designCues.use: Put a tonal scoring-slash graphic on the back yoke and the bacterium story on the inside label. This is science, not a trademark.

designCues.cue: Crinkled burrito foil: mirror-silver foil with soft hand-folded creases
designCues.source: Mission taquerías' foil-wrapped burritos
designCues.use: Use foil-print packaging and hangtags or reflective crinkle trim on a limited Mission drop made with Calle 24 or La Cocina partners.

designCues.cue: Hand-painted storefront lettering: brush script and drop-shadow block letters in red, green and yellow
designCues.source: Taquería, panadería and produce-market signs on Mission Street, 24th Street and International Boulevard
designCues.use: Commission working Bay sign painters to letter names and numbers for Mission or Fruitvale drops, and credit and pay them.

designCues.cue: La Vic's orange sauce: the bright, creamy chili-orange of San Jose's cult taquería sauce
designCues.source: La Victoria Taqueria, downtown San Jose
designCues.use: Use it as a South Bay accent on navy for a San Jose drop. Use the name or bottle only under license from La Victoria.

designCues.cue: T Third route line: a single line from Chinatown–Rose Pak through Chase Center to Bayview, with food-stop dots
designCues.source: Muni's T Third line and the Central Subway
designCues.use: Draw an original route-map graphic for shooting shirts and tees. Do not use the Muni 'worm' logo or SFMTA marks without a license.

productHooks: T Line Table capsule: a shooting shirt and tee with an original route graphic from Chinatown–Rose Pak through Chase Center to Bayview's Third Street, launched with paid collab menu items from a Chinatown bakery and a Bayview kitchen, running from Lunar New Year (Feb 6, 2027) through Black History Month.

Crab Feed holiday pack for the Dec 25 game against Denver: a navy fleece with cooked-crab orange (#D4502A) and shell-cream accents, a bib-shaped hangtag and butcher-paper-print packaging, with part of the proceeds funding a community crab feed through Eat. Learn. Play. or an Oakland or Bayview nonprofit.
Dutch Crunch pregame hoodie: a crackle emboss on Warriors gold (#FFC72C), a sourdough-scoring tonal back graphic and the 'named for the city' bacterium story on the inside label.
Ube and gold Filipino Heritage Night capsule for October, co-designed with Filipino-American Bay artists, with a Señor Sisig pop-up at Thrive City and retail in Daly City and Vallejo.
Town Table Oakland drop: released only at a Lake Merritt or Fruitvale pop-up, co-created with Everett & Jones and International Boulevard truck owners, and lettered by Oakland sign painters.
Foil Pack regional tees: a Mission version in crinkle-foil packaging made with Calle 24 and La Cocina chefs, and a San Jose version with a licensed La Vic's orange accent.
watchouts: Every business named here (La Taqueria, La Victoria, Mitchell's, Thanh Long, Boudin, Señor Sisig) owns its name and look, so license, credit and pay it. Do not use Muni's 'worm' logo or other SFMTA marks without permission.

The Mission and Bayview have lived through tech-era displacement, and the move to a pricier San Francisco arena is part of that story. Partner through community groups (Calle 24, La Cocina, Bayview organizations), price for access, and keep Día de los Muertos altar and procession imagery off product.
Oakland still hurts from the 2019 move. Oakland product should be made with Oakland businesses and sold in Oakland, not offered as a nostalgia graphic at Chase Center.

Athlete food ventures (Ayesha Curry's brands, Gentleman's Cut bourbon, Butler's Bigface Coffee) are separate IP tied to endorsement deals. Confirm Stephen Curry's and Jimmy Butler's current footwear and apparel partners, and keep alcohol references off youth product.
Bay restaurants open and close quickly, and the Dungeness opener moves from year to year. Reconfirm every partner before committing, and never date-lock product to the crab season.

verify: Chase Center's 2026-27 concessions operator and local restaurant lineup, which Thrive City restaurants are open, and whether Thrive City will host road-game watch parties this season.

Stephen Curry's current footwear and apparel partner (he ended his Under Armour deal in late 2025; new partner unconfirmed) and Jimmy Butler's current shoe deal, before any athlete-linked food collab.
Dates and formats of the Warriors' 2026-27 Filipino Heritage Night, Lunar New Year night and Black History Month games.
Opening date of the 2026-27 Dungeness crab commercial season for the San Francisco area (recent openers have been delayed).
Whether the 2026-27 City Edition or the Warriors' Specter uniforms already use Chinatown, Lunar New Year or food references, so a capsule doesn't repeat them.
Lunar New Year 2027 falls on Feb 6; confirm the dates of the 2027 San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade and San Jose Tết festival.
That the T Third still runs from Chinatown–Rose Pak to Bayview via the UCSF/Chase Center stop (SFMTA has adjusted service patterns since 2023).
That Old Skool Cafe (Bayview) is still operating, and which Everett & Jones Barbeque locations in Oakland are open.
Operating status of Señor Sisig, Reem's California, and Nelson German's alaMar and Sobre Mesa, plus Tanya Holland's current ventures.
Current status of the Curry family's food ventures: Sweet July, Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation programs and Gentleman's Cut.
Dates of the 2027 Black Joy Parade and of Carnaval San Francisco 2027 (Memorial Day weekend).
That La Taqueria, La Victoria Taqueria, Mitchell's Ice Cream, Thanh Long, Swan Oyster Depot and Mister Jiu's are still operating, and who handles licensing for La Victoria's orange-sauce name.

culture.headline: The Bay prides itself on inventing and rebuilding (San Francisco's flag is a phoenix), but the Warriors' heart is still Oakland, which lost three teams in five years, and 'Golden State' is the regional name that must hold The Town, The City and San Jose together.
culture.summary: The Bay sees itself as the place that invents the future and rebuilds after disaster: San Francisco flies a phoenix rising from flames, and the region gave the country the Free Speech Movement, the Black Panther Party, the rainbow flag and Silicon Valley. The rest of the country, locals feel, sees tech money and 'doom loop' headlines, while Oakland, which lost the Warriors (2019), Raiders (2020) and A's (2024), carries an Oakland-vs-everybody chip that still shapes how fans read anything stamped 'San Francisco'. 'Golden State' is a regional name by design, for a franchise that has played in San Francisco, Daly City, Oakland and San Jose, and it serves six area codes and one of the most Asian American fan bases in the league. The 2026-27 season lands on a stack of anniversaries (the Panthers' 60th this month, the Bay Bridge's 90th in November, 'We Believe' at 20 next spring), so Nike's opening is to tell them from inside each community, in gear built for fog and rain.

insights.title: Oakland lost three teams in five years
insights.detail: The Warriors played 47 seasons in Oakland (1971-2019) before moving to Chase Center in Mission Bay, the Raiders left for Las Vegas in 2020 and the A's played their last Coliseum game in September 2024. The 2015, 2017 and 2018 title parades ran down Broadway to Lake Merritt; the 2022 parade went down Market Street in San Francisco.
insights.implication: Treat Oakland as the fan base's emotional core, not a heritage footnote: make Oakland pieces with Oakland creators and sell them in Oakland before Chase Center. Product that only says 'San Francisco' reads as the team that left.

insights.title: 'Golden State' is a regional name by design
insights.detail: The franchise arrived from Philadelphia in 1962 as the San Francisco Warriors, took the Golden State name when it moved to Oakland in 1971, spent 1996-97 at San Jose Arena while Oakland's arena was rebuilt, and kept the name when it crossed back to San Francisco. San Jose, at roughly a million people, is the Bay's biggest city, yet the 408 and the Peninsula rarely see themselves on Warriors product.
insights.implication: Build identity around the whole Bay (area codes, the bay's shape, the bridges) and give San Jose and the Peninsula their own releases. 'Golden State' lets one product speak to Oakland, San Francisco and the South Bay without picking a side.

insights.title: Inventors and rebuilders, not the 'doom loop'
insights.detail: Locals see the Bay as where things start (the Gold Rush, the 1964 Free Speech Movement, the 1968 San Francisco State strike that created ethnic studies, Pride, Silicon Valley) and as a place that rebuilds: San Francisco's flag shows a phoenix over 'Oro en Paz, Fierro en Guerra' (gold in peace, iron in war). They feel the country sees tech wealth, 'doom loop' San Francisco and crime-story Oakland, and Joe Lacob's 'light-years ahead' quote made the Warriors look like Silicon Valley's team.
insights.implication: Lead with invention-and-resilience stories told by locals, and keep tech-bro tropes and urban-decline imagery off product. The phoenix motto is a ready identity line for a team called the Golden State Warriors.

insights.title: 2026-27 lands on an anniversary stack
insights.detail: The Black Panther Party was founded in Oakland on October 15, 1966 (60 years this month), the Bay Bridge opened on November 12, 1936 (90), and the 8th-seeded 'We Believe' Warriors beat 67-win Dallas in spring 2007 (20). The Golden Gate Bridge turns 90 on May 27, 2027, the same year as the Summer of Love's 60th.
insights.implication: Bay Bridge 90 (the bridge in the logo) and We Believe 20 are product moments; Panthers 60 is a moment to listen and fund, not to merchandise. After a 37-45 season and a 40.5 win total, an underdog-heritage story suits this roster better than title talk.

insights.title: One of the NBA's most Asian American fan bases
insights.detail: Asian Americans are more than a third of San Francisco and of Santa Clara County; the Bay holds the country's oldest Chinatown, Daly City's large Filipino American community, SoMa Pilipinas next to Mission Bay, and San Jose's Little Saigon. Palo Alto's Jeremy Lin began his NBA career at Oracle, and the Warriors' Lunar New Year and Filipino Heritage nights are core dates, not niche ones.
insights.implication: Asian American heritage product is core business here. Co-create Lunar New Year (Year of the Goat, February 6, 2027), Filipino American History Month (October) and Vietnamese American work with community institutions, and skip generic dragons and lanterns.

insights.title: The Black Bay is being priced out, and remembers it
insights.detail: The Fillmore was the 'Harlem of the West' until redevelopment cleared it from the 1950s on; San Francisco's Black share has fallen from about 13% in 1970 to about 5%, and Oakland's from nearly half in 1980 to about a fifth. Bayview-Hunters Point, San Francisco's remaining Black neighborhood, connects straight to Chase Center on the T Third light rail.
insights.implication: Co-author Black History Month and Juneteenth work with institutions such as Marcus Books and the Bayview Opera House, and send money back into those neighborhoods. The T line is a literal route for a Bayview-to-Chase activation.

insights.title: Dress for microclimates, not seasons
insights.detail: Summer fog holds San Francisco in the 50s and 60s while the East Bay and San Jose bake, September and October are the city's real summer, and the NBA season runs through the wet months of atmospheric-river storms. Locals live in layers: a fleece or quarter-zip under a light shell, hood up, almost never a heavy parka.
insights.implication: Build fan apparel as a layering system (packable water-repellent shells, midweight fleece, vests) cut to go over a jersey on BART, Muni and Caltrain and at Thrive City watch parties. The Patagonia vest is the tech uniform locals mock, so don't style toward it.

places.name: Lake Merritt
places.why: The Town's front porch: the 2015-2018 title parades ended beside it, weekend vendors and drummers fill it, and 2018's 'BBQ'n While Black' cookout turned a viral incident into Oakland pride.

places.name: McClymonds High School
places.why: 'The School of Champions' produced Bill Russell, Frank Robinson, Curt Flood and Vada Pinson, which makes it the root of Oakland's sports lineage and a grassroots partner where investment would be noticed.

places.name: Marcus Books
places.neighborhood: North Oakland (Martin Luther King Jr. Way)
places.why: Founded in San Francisco's Fillmore in 1960 and widely called the oldest Black-owned bookstore in the country, its Oakland store is a living archive for Black History Month programming.

places.name: Fruitvale
places.why: Oakland's Latino heart around Fruitvale BART and International Boulevard, home to one of the Bay's biggest Día de los Muertos festivals.

places.name: Calle 24 Latino Cultural District
places.why: 24th Street, designated a Latino cultural district in 2014, is the Mission's commercial spine and Carnaval's home turf, and the reference point for Latino Heritage work in The City.

places.name: SoMa Pilipinas
places.why: A Filipino cultural heritage district a short walk from Chase Center, marking a community South of Market has housed for generations; the natural partner for Filipino Heritage Night and October's Filipino American History Month.

places.name: Chinese Historical Society of America Museum
places.why: Housed in Julia Morgan's former Chinatown YWCA, it documents the country's oldest Chinatown and is the right collaborator to keep Lunar New Year product specific.

places.name: Bayview Opera House
places.why: San Francisco's oldest theater (1888) and the Bayview's cultural center, on the T Third line that runs straight to Chase Center.

places.name: Little Saigon (Story Road)
places.why: San Jose has more Vietnamese Americans than any other U.S. city, and Story Road is their commercial heart, a South Bay community Warriors product rarely speaks to.

places.name: Cow Palace
places.why: The San Francisco Warriors' 1960s home, and a venue that hosted Warriors home playoff games during the 1975 title run: the forgotten city in the franchise story.

people.name: Stephen and Ayesha Curry
people.role: Warriors franchise star; co-founders of the Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation
people.why: Their foundation has centered Oakland kids since 2019, the clearest sign that the franchise's face still invests in The Town. Curry left Under Armour in late 2025 and his next apparel partner is unconfirmed, so any likeness work needs a deal check first.

people.name: Al Attles (1937-2024)
people.role: Warriors guard, 1975 title coach and franchise lifer
people.why: 'The Destroyer' spent more than six decades with the franchise across Philadelphia, San Francisco and Oakland, and was one of the first Black head coaches to win an NBA title.

people.name: Bill Russell (1934-2022)
people.role: Hall of Famer raised in Oakland
people.why: A McClymonds High and University of San Francisco product who won NCAA titles at USF in 1955 and 1956 before his 11 Celtics rings, he anchors the Bay's claim to basketball's foundations.

people.name: Baron Davis
people.role: Point guard of the 2007 'We Believe' Warriors
people.why: The face of the 8-seed upset of 67-win Dallas at Oracle; with Stephen Jackson and teammates, the natural co-authors of a 20th-anniversary story.

people.name: Gary Payton
people.role: Hall of Fame point guard from Oakland's Skyline High
people.why: The loudest symbol of Oakland's point-guard lineage (with Jason Kidd and Damian Lillard), and the father of current Warrior Gary Payton II, which gives a Town-lineage story a live link to this roster.

people.name: Ryan Coogler
people.role: Filmmaker, born in Oakland and raised in Richmond
people.why: From 'Fruitvale Station' (about Oscar Grant's 2009 killing at Fruitvale BART) to opening 'Black Panther' in 1992 Oakland, he is the East Bay's most powerful storyteller, a creative partner who would expect real authorship.

people.name: Sogorea Te' Land Trust
people.role: Indigenous women-led land trust in the East Bay, co-founded by Corrina Gould (Lisjan Ohlone)
people.why: Its Shuumi Land Tax is the Bay's best-known model for honoring Ohlone land, and it is the right first call before any Native American Heritage work.

people.name: Jeremy Lin
people.why: The Palo Alto High alum's 'Linsanity' run is the defining Asian American NBA story, and it began with home-crowd roars at Oracle; a resonant voice for Asian American heritage work if available.

moments.name: Black Panther Party founding, 60th anniversary
moments.why: Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale founded the party in Oakland in 1966; commemorations fall in the season's opening weeks, a moment for Nike to fund and amplify Panther-led programs rather than sell imagery.

moments.name: Bay Bridge 90th anniversary
moments.why: The bridge in the Warriors logo opened in 1936, six months before the Golden Gate, and its eastern span was rebuilt after a section collapsed in the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake; the date falls during NBA Cup group play.

moments.name: Christmas night: Nuggets at Warriors
moments.why: ESPN/ABC's nightcap puts Chase Center in national prime time, and Denver's Aaron Gordon (Archbishop Mitty, San Jose) comes home; the best night of the year to show the whole Bay on product.

moments.name: Lunar New Year and the San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade
moments.timing: Lunar New Year is February 6, 2027 (Year of the Goat); the parade follows within weeks
moments.why: A Chinatown tradition dating to the 1860s and one of the largest of its kind outside Asia, paired each season with a Warriors Lunar New Year game.

moments.name: Cesar Chavez Day
moments.why: A California state holiday for the organizer who learned his craft in East San Jose's Sal Si Puedes barrio, and the South Bay's clearest Latino civic touchstone.

moments.name: 'We Believe' 20th anniversary
moments.why: Twenty years since the 8-seed Warriors beat 67-win Dallas in six games before a roaring Oracle crowd, the Oakland fan base's favorite memory, arriving just as the 2027 playoffs start.

moments.name: Bay to Breakers
moments.why: San Francisco's costumed 12K from the Embarcadero to Ocean Beach, run since 1912, is the city's weirdest and most self-aware civic ritual and a natural running tie-in.

moments.name: San Francisco Pride
moments.why: One of the world's largest Pride celebrations, in the city where Harvey Milk was elected and Gilbert Baker made the rainbow flag in 1978; it lands around NBA Draft week.
